question: True or false: musicians with perfect pitch can be worse than others at naming intervals in an unusual key?
answer: True. Ken'ichi Miyazaki had musicians name intervals, the distance between two notes, set in C or in out-of-tune keys. Those with perfect pitch did well in C but slipped badly in the odd keys, while listeners who judged by relative pitch stayed steady. They had been reading note names, not hearing distances.
move: A strong shortcut can starve the slower skill it replaces.
ask: Which shortcut of mine works so well that I have stopped building the skill underneath?
trap: Assuming a rarer, stronger pitch skill wins at every pitch task.
reference: Miyazaki, Absolute pitch as an inability: identification of musical intervals in a tonal context, Music Perception, 1993
